exposure: high infant gut microbiota alpha diversity
cohort: 465 infants with bacterial 16S rRNA V4-V5 gene sequencing data and 185 infants with shotgun metagenomics data
finding: Higher infant gut microbiota alpha diversity at six weeks of age was associated with an increased risk of infections and respiratory symptoms, particularly upper respiratory tract infections.
mod_finding: Among vaginally delivered infants, higher alpha diversity was associated with an increased risk of wheezing and diarrhea, while among cesarean-delivered infants, it was associated with an increased risk of Haemophilus influenzae infection.
